transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-06-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Sara Liu (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Emily Chen (Novus Head of Security), Tom Barker (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Product Manager)

[00:00] Sara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I’m Sara, AE at Redwood, Diego our solutions engineer is with me. How are you all?
[00:15] Emily: Good, thanks. Quick context, we're evaluating Redwood for embedding clinical note summarization, but security and least-priv access is our blocker.
[00:28] Sara: Totally. Today's agenda is SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC model, audit logs, and encryption/KMS — any other must-haves?
[00:35] Priya: Nope, that's the list. We'll want to understand how group-based roles map and how fast we can onboard 60 users.
[01:05] Diego: Cool. High level — we support SAML 2.0 IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Ping, etc.), SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. For RBAC we expose roles at the org and project level and you can map SCIM groups to roles.
[01:38] Tom: Quick question — can we enforce SSO-only login and still have service accounts for API calls? We want token rotation controls.
[01:50] Diego: Yes, you can enforce SSO for interactive logins. API tokens are separate and you can scope them and rotate them; we have token expiry and you can tie token creation to admin roles only.
[02:10] Emily: Audit logging — we need full event logs for user changes, role assignments, and API access. Retention policy is important (we keep logs 3 years on our SIEM). Will Redwood export logs to our Splunk?
[02:25] Sara: We support syslog / HTTP log export and S3 delivery. For Splunk you can forward from S3 or directly to an HTTP endpoint; we’ve done Splunk integrations. We'll share details.
[02:48] Priya: Also SOC 2 and ISO — can you send the attestation and the scope? We need to confirm data handling for PHI-ish metadata.
[02:58] Sara: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates and the controls mapping. Note: we are not a BAA provider by default; you asked specifically about PHI earlier?
[03:12] Emily: We're not storing raw PHI in Redwood, but clinical metadata could be PII-ish. We'll need to confirm encryption in transit and at rest and customer-managed keys.
[03:28] Diego: On encryption we encrypt at rest; for customer-managed keys (CMK) we support KMS integrations on Private deployments and Dedicated via KMS/HSM options. For hosted we have managed encryption keys but RTP (bring-your-own-key) on Dedicated/Private.
[03:50] Tom: For pilot we'd probably go with hosted but need to know if we can store certain logs/residency in EU region. Data residency?
[03:58] Sara: We have region selection for hosted and you can pin an org to a region for data residency. We'll confirm available regions for your account.
[04:12] Priya: SCIM specifics — do you support group-to-role mapping and incremental syncs? Our IdP is Okta and we use group membership to assign roles.
[04:25] Diego: Yes. SCIM 2.0 group push supported. Mapping is configurable — you can map Okta group names to Redwood roles, and we support delta syncs. Note: sometimes attribute names differ, so we recommend a test setup.
[04:50] Emily: Are there known gotchas? Anything customers trip on?
[04:56] Diego: Two things — claims mapping for SAML (email vs userPrincipalName), and SCIM group naming mismatches. Also make sure your IdP sends the group claim or use a group push.
[05:12] Tom: Can we do delegated admin? We want limited admins for infra and separate product admins.
[05:18] Diego: Absolutely. Roles can be created with granular permissions — admin, billing_admin, org_viewer, project_writer, etc. We can show a sample least-privilege role matrix.
[05:34] Priya: How are RBAC changes audited? We need an immutable trail for compliance.
[05:40] Sara: All role changes, user provisioning events, and token creations are logged; audit logs include actor, timestamp, IP, action, and resource. We also support log signing and shipping to your SIEM.
[06:02] Emily: Is there an API for pulling audit logs or do we need to ingest the exported files?
[06:08] Diego: There's an audit API for recent events (last 90 days) and we recommend S3 export for long-term retention.
[06:22] Tom: For KMS, you mentioned bring-your-own-key on Dedicated. For hosted, can we rotate keys or get customer-managed encryption?
[06:33] Diego: Hosted uses managed keys; Dedicated/Private can be configured with your KMS. Rotation is supported on Dedicated with HSM-backed keys.
[06:45] Priya: For SCIM provisioning, would you recommend group push or SCIM sync?
[06:52] Diego: If you use Okta, group push is easiest. SCIM incremental sync works too but group push reduces mapping friction.
[07:05] Emily: We need SSO bindings tested end-to-end — who would do that?
[07:11] Sara: We can run a guided setup, Diego will do the technical setup with Tom, and we'll verify claims and SCIM flow.
[07:20] Diego: I'll send a checklist — metadata fields we need (EntityID, ACS URL, NameID format, required attributes like email, given_name, family_name).
[07:33] Tom: NameID — we use email primarily. We also need SCIM to include group membership in the payload.
[07:40] Diego: Ok, we'll show you the expected SCIM schema and example payloads.
[08:02] Priya: On roles, we want a default least-privilege template for product and infra.
[08:09] Diego: We'll provide a template: org_admin (manage org settings), infra_admin (manage deployments), billing_admin, viewer, integrator (API only). You can customize policies per project.
[08:25] Emily: For security review, we will need to show the auditors how RBAC is enforced and how account changes are logged — any way to demo this quickly?
[08:34] Diego: We can provide a short recording or a live walkthrough that shows role assignment -> audit event -> log export to S3. We can also share the schema of the audit event.
[08:50] Tom: Do you support SCIM bulk deprovisioning? We need to be able to revoke access for 100+ users quickly if needed.
[08:58] Diego: Yes, group removal triggers deprovision events; we also support bulk deprovision API.
[09:10] Emily: About retention — if we export logs to our SIEM, what's guaranteed in Redwood?
[09:18] Sara: We keep logs for X days in the platform for search (we'll confirm exact retention), but for audit-grade retention you should export to your SIEM/S3. We will share the exact retention numbers for hosted vs Dedicated.
[09:40] Priya: Any integration for SCIM with AD via Okta? We currently have AD -> Okta -> SCIM flow.
[09:48] Diego: That's a common pattern and works fine. Okta becomes the IdP and you push groups from AD into Okta, then Okta pushes to Redwood.
[10:02] Tom: On encryption of logs in transit, do you support TLS mutual auth to the collector?
[10:09] Sara: We support TLS; mutual TLS for log ingestion can be discussed as part of an enterprise integration. We'll note that as a potential option.
[10:22] Emily: Data residency follow-up — can we keep data and logs in EU?
[10:29] Sara: Yes, we can region-pin an org to EU; we'll confirm the operational tradeoffs.
[10:38] Priya: For the pilot, timeline-wise, we want SSO + SCIM onboarding in two weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[10:44] Diego: Yes, for 60 users with group push and Okta it's doable; we'll need metadata and a test IdP, plus one or two test users.
[11:05] Tom: Will Redwood accept our IdP attributes? We use custom attributes for role tags sometimes.
[11:13] Diego: We can map custom attributes if the IdP sends them; otherwise use group mapping.
[11:26] Emily: Are session length and SSO session timeouts configurable? We need session timeouts aligned with our SSO policy.
[11:34] Diego: Yes, session timeout can be controlled by us and often enforced via IdP SAML assertions. We can set defaults and honor the IdP session if configured.
[11:56] Priya: Compliance artifacts — can you provide control mappings to our auditors?
[12:03] Sara: Yes, we provide a controls mapping doc and our SOC 2/ISO artifacts under NDA or via an auditor portal.
[12:20] Emily: How about SCIM rate limits — we sync groups periodically, but we need to ensure we don't hit throttling during mass changes.
[12:28] Diego: SCIM has rate limits; for large deprovisions we advise using the bulk API or coordinate with us and we can temporarily increase limits for the pilot.
[12:45] Tom: Regarding API keys and service accounts, can you require MFA for admin actions?
[12:51] Diego: We support MFA for interactive users via SSO/IdP policy. For API keys, we recommend short-lived tokens and automations for rotation; some enterprise setups use a gateway that enforces additional MFA.
[13:12] Priya: Is there fine-grained permission for dataset access inside a project? We want to make sure only certain roles can access sensitive corpora.
[13:20] Diego: Yes, dataset-level permissions exist; you can control who can read/write and which roles can create endpoints.
[13:35] Emily: Any default admin accounts we should watch for?
[13:40] Sara: You get one initial org_owner during setup; we recommend immediately assigning least-priv roles and creating a break-glass admin with approval gating.
[13:55] Tom: For the pilot we'll need the RBAC JSON schema to import programmatically.
[14:02] Diego: We'll provide example JSON and CLI snippets.
[14:20] Priya: Testing — when we do the test, do you provide a staging org?
[14:27] Sara: Yes, we can provision a trial org pinned to your region. We'll coordinate.
[14:40] Emily: One last question on KMS — if we go Dedicated during pilot, what's the earliest that BYOK can be enabled?
[14:48] Diego: BYOK for Dedicated needs a short provisioning window; typically a couple weeks, but for pilot we can do hosted then transition.
[15:05] Sara: Ok quick recap — action items and docs we'll share: SAML metadata and ACS URL, SCIM schema and example payloads, RBAC role matrix and JSON examples, SOC2/ISO artifacts, audit log export options.
[15:22] Priya: That works. We'll get IdP details to Tom and Emily will confirm audit needs.
[15:35] Sara: Great — Diego will set up the follow-up technical session. Thanks all.
[15:45] Emily: Thanks everyone.

[End of transcript]
